title: Messy data the model must reason over? Move work from model to code
head: Situation
Right mechanism
Why
rows: Model only ever sees one format
A yes/no fact derived from data
No arithmetic left to the model
Converter exists and its call is enforced
Deterministic if the call can't be skipped
Model must choose among formats occasionally, errors tolerable
rule: Normalise in a hook and compute derived facts in the tool. Anything the model must remember to do is still probabilistic.

title: A policy keeps being broken: does it need judgement or a hard stop?
head: What you observe
Where the fault is
Fix
rows: Rule must hold every time (control failure, legal)
Goal is fewer wrong calls, judgement involved
Explicit criteria plus a few examples
Need to know afterwards what happened
One tool must run before the others
Gate, or forced tool_choice on that request
Tool results arrive in mixed formats
rule: When a rule must hold every time, put it in code that runs before the action. Prompts improve behaviour; hooks guarantee it.

title: Model gets numbers wrong: is the job deterministic?
head: Situation
Right mechanism
Why
rows: A few fixed formats (dates, signs, decimals)
Exact parse, model never sees ambiguity
rule: Hooks normalise fixed formats at the boundary; tools compute values from real sources. Leave to the model only what code can't decide.

title: A hook exists but the policy is still broken: what does the hook actually check?
head: What you observe
Where the fault is
Fix
rows: Limit broken by several small calls without any rejection
Hook checks per call, policy is per total
Hook sums the running total, blocks and escalates
Agent retries the same call after a rejection
Error gives no category or retry signal
Hard rule written only in the prompt
Move the rule into a hook
Borderline judgment about when to hand off
One tool doing two different jobs
rule: A hook enforces only what it checks. If the policy is about a total, the hook must check the total.

title: Messy tool data: where can you fix it?
head: What you observe
Where the fault is
Fix
rows: Messy formats from a server you run
Messy formats from a server you don't control
Nothing on your side cleans it
PostToolUse hook normalizes results before the model sees them
Tool results bloated with irrelevant fields
Trim results to the relevant fields
An action must be blocked every time
Hook that intercepts the outgoing call
Readers misread old vs new figures
rule: Fix data where you control it. For tool results you don't own, normalize them in a PostToolUse hook before the model sees them.

title: Sensitive or messy tool data? Ask where to change it
head: Situation
Right mechanism
Why
rows: Model must never use a field; server can't change
Model should usually phrase things a certain way
You own the tool and the field isn't needed
Stop returning it from the tool
Results arrive in mixed formats (dates, codes)
An action must be blocked (refund over limit)
rule: Must never use the data? Strip it from the tool result with a PostToolUse hook, before the model reads it.

title: Which control acts at the right moment?
head: Goal
Mechanism
When it acts
rule: To stop an action, intercept the outgoing call. PostToolUse is for results.
